comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C discuss average deposit and loan volumes within their Wealth/Consumer segments, highlighting client migration to higher-yielding investment alternatives as a key driver for deposit declines. BAC reports a $10.8 billion decrease in average deposits driven by this shift, while C reports a 2% increase in average deposits (net of $17 billion in transfers from USPB) but acknowledges a partial offset from a shift to higher-yielding investments on its platform. Conversely, BAC reports a $4.4 billion increase in average loans driven by custom lending and residential mortgages, whereas C reports a 1% decrease in average loans as the business optimized capital usage.

sentences.text: Average loans increased $4.4 billion to $223.9 billion, primarily driven by custom lending and residential mortgage loans.

Average deposits decreased $10.8 billion to $287.5 billion primarily driven by clients moving deposits to higher yielding investment cash alternatives, including offerings on our investment and brokerage platforms.

Average deposits increased 2%, reflecting the transfers of relationships and the associated deposits from USPB ($17 billion at the time of transfer over the last 12 months), partially offset by a shift in deposits to higher-yielding investments on Citi's platform.
Average loans decreased 1%, as Wealth continued to optimize capital usage.

comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM report increases in lending volumes within their respective wealth or consumer banking operations. BAC’s Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) segment saw average loans increase $4.4 billion to $223.9 billion, primarily driven by custom lending and residential mortgage loans. Similarly, JPM’s overall loan portfolio increased $19.8 billion, with specific growth noted in securities-based lending within its Asset & Wealth Management (AWM) segment. Both disclosures identify custom/lending types (custom lending for BAC, securities-based lending for JPM) as key growth drivers in these segments.
